slashJoinerAudit.measured: The subject contains one slashJoiner mention, in basedOn.namedCatalog.role — 'Named the live G20 v1 corpus classes and carried slashJoiner.' It carries no slashJoiner field and no slash-joiner sentence of its own. G20 v1 carries two such fields and the catalog carries six mentions.
slashJoinerAudit.whyThisIsNotADefect: Four reasons, and I checked each rather than accepting the first. First, the guard's purpose — keeping 'human/JSON/SARIF/doctor/fault/config/progress/log' as one slash-joined surface set rather than eight classes — is structurally preserved here, because the join's namedCorpusNotAuthored is a one-element list whose single element is that whole phrase. There is no route by which a reader of this artifact counts eight classes. Second, the join points at where the guard lives and pins that artifact by digest, so the discipline is reachable from pinned material. Third, the catalog's own findingDisposition shows the slash-joiner discipline was a SHOULD-FIX landed at catalog v2 in classes[0].slashJoinerVerbatim and classes[0].surfacesInOrder — so the corpus deliberately sited that content in the catalog, and the join's job is to consume the naming rather than restate it. Fourth, and decisively on consistency: sdk-leftover-join.v1 contained zero slashJoiner mentions and I accepted it at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. v2 has strictly more. Raising this now would be moving the bar between a predecessor and its successor on unchanged ground.

Four of the five Claude-lane verdicts this artifact pins are my own work: the G20 v1 harness review, the sdk-leftover-join v1 review, and — by lane — the v4 and catalog reviews. Most directly, I accepted the v1 predecessor of this very subject at 0/0. That creates two opposite risks and I handled them separately. The risk of going soft I answered by re-deriving rather than carrying forward: the three-way named-list equality, the reservedVerbatim comparison, the upstream OBL-* cross-check and every digest were computed against the artifacts in this cycle, not inherited from the v1 review. I record that reasoning in full so a coordinator can check whether I applied a consistent bar rather than a convenient one.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-two attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 8782e497 at 0444, 15571 bytes, unmoved at both ends; predecessor v1 unmoved at 86c45093 and not overwritten; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; live DR-125 token OPEN and the live DR-G20 owner cell both matching what the subject states; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All twelve cited pins reproduce and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head. All six cited verdicts are exact, including the dual ACCEPT 0/0 D-110 records for v4. The novelty of v2 is the claim that the naming half is closed, so I tested the equality behind it rather than reading it: G20 v1's namedCorpusNotAuthored, the catalog's, and the join's are the identical single-element list. The distinction the dispatch protects is held at the point where conflating it would have been easiest — OBL-G20-NAMED-CATALOG is leftoverDesign false and says in terms that it is not leftover-design of fixture implementations and does not close OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING, while that obligation stays leftoverDesign true and separates authoring from the specification, the catalog and execution. The dispatch's slashJoiner attack does not land. The join carries one slashJoiner mention against the catalog's six, but the guard's purpose — keeping the eight slash-joined surfaces as one class — is structurally preserved by a one-element list, the catalog that holds the discipline is pinned by digest, the catalog's own findingDisposition shows that content was deliberately sited there by a landed finding, and decisively the v1 predecessor I accepted at 0/0 contained zero slashJoiner mentions, so escalating at v2 would move the bar on unchanged ground. I also ran the completeness test that produced a blocker on the DR-105 join: every OBL-* named upstream in G20 v1 or the catalog — four of them — is carried here, and reservedVerbatim equals v4's reserved array as an ordered list of six. One shape recurred and was traced rather than reported: the D-110 honesty observations are cited as CLAUDE-V4-O1/O2/O3 while the v4 review's own ids are O-1 through O-4, which is the same qualify-rename discipline I confirmed at D-108 and D-115, with the adopted COORD entry carrying the subject's exact sentence. The successor delta is tight — one obligation added, one amended, seven untouched, none removed — and reconciliation is nine and nine with flags matching buckets. Two things I declined to raise are recorded in full so the bar can be checked: a duplicated clause-5 sentence inside OBL-G20-FX-AUTHORING, which reads as append-without-pruning but states nothing false, and a loose phrase calling this artifact the later leftover-join when v1 first filled that gap, which the pinned predecessor two entries away resolves. One disclosure: four of the five Claude-lane verdicts this artifact pins are my own work, including my acceptance of its immediate predecessor, so I re-derived every measurement in this cycle rather than inheriting it, and I have set out why I did not escalate slashJoiner so a coordinator can judge whether the bar was consistent rather than convenient.
